note.description: Why this is encoded the way it is

items.description: A flat mechanical contribution this content makes to a stat

contributions.description: Every flat mechanical change this item makes to a stat (ADR-029). This is the ONE numeric encoding: the older `statBonus` shape — a bare per-copy map with no target, duration or expression amounts — was a strict subset of it, and two encodings summed independently by the same derivation is a double-count waiting to be authored.

items.description: A single mechanical effect applied when a choice option is selected

appliedEffects.description: Trait/damage/range effects this item applies unconditionally (ADR-029). Same vocabulary as a choice option’s `effects`, declared directly on the record for grants that are not a choice. Named `appliedEffects`, not `effects`: that key is already taken on meta entities with a different `{ label, value }` shape (see getEffects), and one field name meaning two things is how a schema rots.
